To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Smart City technical standard is needed to guide the development and implementation of Smart City technologies.
the solution to the integration problem in Smart Cities is to establish a formalized accepted managed technology regulated environment.

Smart City managers must develop a technical standard for Smart City development that will guide the development and use of autonomous software agents and automated components, and that the standard must be managed by a governance group composed of Smart City managers, citizens, and stake holders, and that it must meet all safety and liability requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a Smart City standard that will enable Smart Cities to function effectively and efficiently.
the development of a framework that can be used for the integration of Smart City components.
establishing technical standards and guidance for the integration of Smart City components, and the development of an integrated Smart City system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the solution to Smart City technical standards and guidance is a formalized and accepted technology regulation introduced by governance groups.

Smart City technical standards are needed to ensure the safety of the citizens and the environment, to ensure the safety and liability of the vendors and developers, and to ensure the safety, liability, and cost effectiveness of the Smart City itself.

the solution to the Smart City integration and management challenge is the establishment of a formalized accepted, and managed technology regulated framework, introduced by governance groups, composed of city planners/ managers, citizens, stake holders, technology delivery organizations, and the general public.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Smart Cities are not a new technology.

the Smart Cities need a formalized technical standard to address the integration problem, and that the standard must be managed by a governance structure composed of city planners, citizen and stakeholders, and technology delivery organization.
a Smart City is an urban area with a high level of automation, a high level of autonomy, and a high level of integration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a technical standard for autonomous systems is necessary and that it must be developed by the Smart City managers and their stakeholders.

Smart Cities need to be managed by a formalized governance group that establishes and manages a Smart City standard and the Smart City technology vendors and developers must be held liable and responsible for the safety of their products.
Smart Cities need to be viewed as a complex system of systems, and a technical standard for Smart City development must be established.
